title: XL tiny house offers apartment-style living on a single floor
desc: By Adam Williams Think tiny house and you'd usually picture compact interiors and space-saving features. However, this XL model spreads out over a single floor to provide two bedrooms, a full-sized kitchen, and a remarkably spacious living area.

title: These electric skis do the skiing for you
desc: By Ben Coxworth Picture this: You're staying at a winter resort and you'd like to explore the local wilderness, but you're not an adept cross-country skier. That's why Snomo was created, as it's a set of Nordic skis (well, sort of) with built-in electric motors.

title: Hibernation provides critical insights into Alzheimer’s disease progress
desc: By Mike McRae As a golden hamster settles into deep hibernation, immune cells within its brain shift into states that look surprisingly familiar to Alzheimer’s disease. New research offers a promising new way to understand the biology of cognitive decline.

title: New 'ghost radar' sees without being seen
desc: By David Szondy BAE Systems' UK-based Digital Intelligence & Land business has developed a "ghost radar" that can see airborne threats, but they can't see it. The new portable stealth system detects and tracks targets without sending out any radio signals of its own.

title: $2,000 electric bike practically teaches you to wheelie
desc: By Utkarsh Sood There was a time when popping a wheelie on a bike required a lot of practice. But what if you could skip much of the learning curve and let the motorcycle do some of the hard work for you? That's where the FRP M3 comes in.

title: Carry-anywhere camp cube bursts open into impressively stocked kitchen
desc: By C.C. Weiss Aiming to create the compact, high-efficiency chuck box alternative it believes the camping and overland world needs, Algorithm Overland presents the Kitchen Cube, a small self-cased kit that folds in an entire kitchen set for 2 to 5 people.

title: Nose drops could boost learning and memory in Alzheimer's patients
desc: By Mike McRae Inspired by a fictitious mouse with surgically enhanced intelligence, researchers have improved memory in aging animals with something considerably less dramatic: nose drops.

title: BMW dreamed up the roofed scooter, now Segway wants a piece
desc: By Utkarsh Sood Segway, one of the world’s most well-known electric scooter brands, is reviving the roofed scooter conversation. The driving factor is, of course, motorcycle safety. So obviously there’s a roll cage … and seatbelts.

title: Articulated gaming mouse wraps your entire finger for instant level up
desc: By Ben Coxworth First of all, never mind how this thing works, get a load of how it looks! That said, the Borslon is in fact claimed to be an improvement on traditional gaming mice, with a radical articulated finger-worn design.

title: You really shouldn’t bother buying your own Tesla Cybercab
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Tesla made a whole lotta noise when it rolled out its steering-wheel-less, pedal-less Cybercab in September. It's now followed that up by inviting a small number of people to buy their own self-driving two-seater. If you got that email, ignore it.

title: 1 platform, 4 motorcycles: Italians take on e-moto modularity
desc: By Utkarsh Sood Why build four bikes when you can build one and give it four personalities? That's essentially the idea behind GR1T, an Italian e-moto startup that's designed four distinct bikes – all sharing the same chassis, motor, battery, and electronics.

title: Apartment-like tiny house feels anything but small inside
desc: By Adam Williams This spacious tiny house has been designed to minimize compromises. It features a remarkably open, apartment-like interior arranged on one floor, with two bedrooms, a generous living area, and plenty of room to move around.

title: Wild hypercar invites you to saddle up and ride 800 horses like a bike
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal An automotive startup in the Netherlands is working on a hypercar with a radically different approach: having the driver sat inside it like they're on a motorcycle, head pitched forward and torso leaned toward the steering wheel.

title: Google taps Quaise’s rock-vaporizing geothermal tech for data center power
desc: By David Szondy Quaise Energy and Google have shaken hands over a world-first agreement for the tech company to purchase 50 MW of continuous power for its data center from Quaise's Project Obsidian super-hot rock geothermal power plant in Oregon.

title: Bunkhouse camping cube claims place among tiniest of tiny homes
desc: By C.C. Weiss VentureXplorer has launched the Bunkr, a tiny, boxy living pod that can become a caravan or stand on its own as a simple tiny home. Either way, it squeezes beds, a full kitchen and a bathroom into one of the smallest tiny-living footprints out there.

title: The world's most striking black and white photos of 2026
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson While we are used to seeing the world around us in vivid color, black and white photography can show us more, not less. This is strikingly clear in winning and finalists' images featured in the fifth edition of the Black & White Photo Awards.

title: Battery-only 19-seater puts China in the electric airliner race
desc: By Omar Kardoudi After 19 flights with nobody aboard, COMAC's 19-seat battery-electric airliner has finally taken a crew up. Now China's aviation regulator is reviewing it for certification, the approval it needs before it can start flying paying passengers.

title: This clever desk turns your sofa into a full-fledged workstation
desc: By Howard Armitage Eleven years, 27 prototypes and one impatient DHL driver. This gloriously overengineered sofa desk uses magnetic trickery to turn your favorite recliner into a fully fledged workstation, without trapping you behind it.

title: 20-ft-long tiny house takes back-to-basics approach to downsizing
desc: By Adam Williams Tiny houses are trending larger and more luxurious, but Dragon Tiny Homes brings things back to basics with a model that's actually tiny – in both size and cost. Named the Aria 20, it's up for sale for $50,695.

title: Darth Vader's lightsaber sets new world record at Star Wars sale
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Star Wars fans hoping to collect a piece of cinematic history at auction needed more than the Force on their side, with Darth Vader's classic lightsaber setting a new world record for props sold from the franchise, going for a cool $4.875 million.

title: Extraterrestrial habitats may rise via Legos of laser-fused moon dust
desc: By Ben Coxworth If astronauts are going to spend much time on the Moon, they need to be able to build permanent structures there. A new technology could help, by allowing them to create Lego-like building blocks from nothing but moon dust.

title: Japan's latest micro-camper is an inexpensive multi-adventuring dream
desc: By C.C. Weiss With its deep, vibrant lineup of kei trucks and vans, Suzuki can definitely hold its own in micro-campers. The new Spacia Base van serves up more evidence, transitioning from a cavernous gear-hauler to a factory micro-camper in a matter of seconds.

title: $1-million bike? Rare 160-hp racebike can't find a single buyer
desc: By Utkarsh Sood The 1978 OW31 is the ultimate factory evolution of Yamaha's TZ750 family: a two-stroke racing monster that helped Johnny Cecotto win the Formula 750 World Championship. Most experts would slap a seven-figure price tag on it. Come auction day, and it went unsold.

title: 'Zero-emission' aluminum production switches up the chemical equation
desc: By Etiido Uko Aluminum, once worth more than gold, is now the world's second-most used metal. Yet its carbon-emitting production process has remained the same for 140 years. Researchers say they have developed a new zero-emission aluminum production process.

title: Low-effort diet boosts lifespan, weight loss and disease protection
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson A short-term "break" that doesn't let you go hungry, the fasting-mimicking diet has been gaining momentum in longevity science thanks to more rigorous findings based on human studies – and how easy it is to stick with to reap the reported benefits.

title: Apollo CAST-1 review: Giving old speakers a new lease on life
desc: By Howard Armitage Apollo's tiny CAST-1 turned a forgotten pair of speakers into a capable Wi-Fi audio system for just US$30. I put it through its paces, and discovered why whole-home audio might finally be worth the fuss.

title: XL tiny house puts a modern twist on farmhouse living
desc: By Adam Williams This XL tiny house offers a comfortable living experience on wheels with fewer compromises than you'd expect. It features a roomy interior with a well-equipped kitchen and is fronted by a nice large porch.

title: Korean magnetic textile cools train tracks to thwart disaster
desc: By Malcolm Azania A fascinating invention from the Korea offers new hope for increased train safety – a heat-shielding textile, magnetically mounted on rails. With its multiple fiberglass and magnetic layers, the textile blocks more than 85% of punishing solar heat.

title: US data centers are burning through as much electricity as entire states
desc: By Mike McRae Between 2024 and 2025, America’s largest data centers used as much electricity as the state of Michigan. If we continue on this path, scientists warn, we'll be on a dangerous path for world health that may be too late to stop.

title: Two new Fender guitars honor George Harrison and... The other Sir Paul
desc: By Barry Divola Fender has celebrated its 80th anniversary in Tokyo with the launch of collaborations with Sir Paul Smith and George Harrison’s estate. We were on the ground to witness the unveiling of the Made in Japan tele and the Dark Horse strat.

title: Eco-friendly ‘plastic’ survives dishwashers but breaks down in nature
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Of the myriad ongoing attempts to create a material that's as versatile as plastic but easily degradable in nature, this one from Shellworks feels like it's awfully close to that dream.

title: RESO Pilot Pro Intercom review: Riding with the new kid on the block
desc: By Utkarsh Sood When it comes to helmet communication systems, Cardo and Sena have largely had the run of the place. Enter RESO, a relatively new name looking to upset that comfortable little arrangement. We review its Pilot Pro intercom after weeks of thorough use.

title: 3-oz multitool delivers vise-like grip and loads of twist
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal The vast majority of multitools that come to our attention are built around blades and screwdrivers. This new one we've just spotted is focused on holding items in place as you work on small repairs and crafts.

title: US air traffic control finally bids farewell to the floppy disk era
desc: By David Szondy The FAA is fast-forwarding the American air traffic control system into the 21st century as it begins a massive modernization program to replace legacy computer systems so old that they depend on 3.5-in floppy disks and vintage programming to operate.

title: Yamaha urges you to ditch the ADV bike and take an ADV scooter instead
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood What if you could go ride off-road without an adventure motorcycle? What if, instead of straddling a tall, intimidating dual-sport, you could do it on a scooter? Yamaha appears to be entertaining exactly that idea with its new RW700 and RW350 scoots.

title: Kestrel-inspired flying robot rides updrafts using wing flaps
desc: Drones Consumer Tech Technology By Ben Coxworth Suppose you wanted a drone that could hover in place like a quadcopter, but that didn't go through batteries nearly as quickly. If you did, you might like Floaty, a "flying robot" that uses moveable wings to ride updrafts.

title: Review: Fender's new Silent Strats are an absolute no-brainer
desc: Music Consumer Tech Technology By Loz Blain It's only taken 72 years, but Fender has finally, comprehensively solved the biggest problem with its most iconic electric guitar: the amount of unwanted noise it makes.

title: Extra-wide tiny house provides a modern take on mountain lodge living
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams With its timber-clad exterior, clean lines, and open layout, the Kodiak offers a modern take on mountain lodge living. The tiny house is arranged on one floor and includes a downstairs bedroom, along with a comfortable living area.

title: Hybrid cargo plane uses electric power to leap off water
desc: Aircraft Transport By Omar Kardoudi Maxwell's M1 Hybrid amphibian pairs electric motors and small diesel engines on the same propellers, saving its battery for hauling a ton of cargo off the water, then flying on engine power to islands and disaster zones with no runway in sight.

title: 5 charming scooters that give Vespa vibes without Vespa prices
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood There’s no denying Vespas have practically cornered the retro-chic market, but their price tag isn't exactly pocket change. But there’s good news: there are several alternatives that borrow from its design playbook without asking you to cough up the premium.

title: Electric work van gains 174 miles of range while you finish your lunch
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall US commercial vehicle manufacturers got a blunt lesson in how far they lag behind the rest of the world when a new French delivery van, virtually unknown outside Europe, is introduced with sophisticated software-defined architecture and 800-V electrics.

title: Historic launch sees 4 strike drones catapulted off British supercarrier
desc: Military Engineering By David Szondy Naval drone warfare reached a historic milestone as four strike drones were launched from the deck of the supercarrier HMS Queen Elizabeth as part of an exercise demonstrating how uncrewed combat aircraft can operate alongside fighter jets and other assets.

title: Common glaucoma test can save eyesight before point of no return
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Scientists are on the brink of a major breakthrough when it comes to the most common form of glaucoma that leads to blindness, with a huge leap forward in the genetic test an international team has been working to perfect for most of the decade.

title: Vibrating TV screen puts people's voices where their mouths are
desc: Electronics Consumer Tech Technology By Etiido Uko Imagine seeing someone's lips move on a screen, but hearing their voice coming from their feet. Researchers at KIMM have developed a display that fixes this disconnect by producing sound directly from the part of the screen where the action happens.

title: Hard-carving snow ebike doubles up on motor and battery power
desc: Outdoors By Ben Coxworth Envo Drive Systems' MoonBike electric snow bike definitely looks like it's a lot fun, but is it up for doing some actual work? Well, for any jobs it can't handle, a new utility version is on the way – and it'll pack double the motor power.

title: Review: The world's first Full HD tri-fold portable projector
desc: Home Entertainment Consumer Tech Technology By Paul Ridden Building on the popularity of its utterly adorable Z-shaped portable projectors, Aurzen launched a Full HD flavor at IFA 2026 in September. I recently got my hands on a Zip Pro, and the on-screen resolution isn't the only spec to get a serio

title: 10,000-watt electric unicycle will test your resolve on and off road
desc: Urban Transport Transport By C.C. Weiss The all-new KingSong F16 Aven electric unicycle sounds like a type of fighter jet and will feel nearly as fast thanks to the 10,000 peak watts powering you over all types of terrain via a single wheel located mere inches from your gennies.

title: Affordable tiny house squeezes the basics into just 16 ft
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams Tiny houses don't come much smaller – or cheaper – than this unnamed model. Measuring just 16 ft long, it features a space-saving interior that makes some interesting choices to maximize its limited footprint.

title: Active winglets... On a 900cc naked bike? What is China smoking?
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood The Tornado Naked Tre 903 Concept is not just Benelli dipping back into its three-cylinder heritage. It features a modular frame and, more intriguingly, a set of active aerodynamic winglets that can move independently depending on the environment.

title: 3D-printed frog swims using artificial muscles powered by light
desc: Technology By Mike McRae A frog that takes nearly two minutes to swim about the length of a credit card is unlikely to make a splash at the next Amphibian Olympics. Then again, most frogs have the benefit of some 200 million years of evolution. This one was just hatched out of a 3D printer.

title: 10-person exo-beam air tent fends off 100-mph+ hurricane winds
desc: Tents Gear Outdoors By C.C. Weiss The latest launch in Heimplanet's iconic inflatable tent family, the Mavericks tent has been fully updated. Already capable of standing strong in 100-mph+ winds, the new version packs in even more toughness and extreme weather-shedding capability.

title: BYD's ultra-fast power stations robo-charge EVs in as few as 5 minutes
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall BYD has combined solar panels, on-site energy storage, superfast Flash Charging and a plug-in robot arm into an extraordinary 'gas station' of the future located in the Abu Dhabi desert.

title: World's fastest passenger liner becomes world's largest artificial reef
desc: By David Szondy In what is both the end of a 74-year career and a new lease on life, the SS United States, the world's fastest transatlantic liner, has been scuttled off the coast of the Florida Panhandle to become the world's largest artificial reef.

title: It's official, Australians have crowned their 2026 Christmas icon
desc: Biology Science By Bronwyn Thompson Move over, Santa in flip-flops holding a cricket bat and a can of beer, the land Down Under has a new favorite Christmas visitor – a stunning golden beetle that will have entomologists more excited than ever. Which says a lot.

title: Jetson ONE personal eVTOL pod is about to go full sky patrol
desc: Aircraft Transport By Omar Kardoudi Florida Polytechnic University says its campus is about to have America's first flying police officer. The department's Jetson ONE, nicknamed Astro, isn't on patrol just yet, but its chief says the FAA has signed off. Now it just needs its papers.

title: Bluetti's expandable home battery tackles a problem I know all too well
desc: Energy Engineering By Howard Armitage I've watched a kettle send my energy monitor soaring, waited through winter mornings for my solar panels to wake up, and wished for a bigger battery in summer. BLUETTI's expandable Apex 200 looks tempting, but is more storage really the answer?

title: Bubble-powered car is ready to take you on an underwater ride
desc: Boats and Watersports Toys Outdoors By Ben Coxworth Ordinarily, if you're in a car that's underwater, that is not a good thing. Such is not the case with the Aquaticar, however, a new amusement-park-ride vehicle which is powered by bubbles.

title: Stroke prevention advances with first-in-class drug approved by FDA
desc: Stroke Brain Health Body and Mind By Bronwyn Thompson A first-of-a-kind daily oral blood thinner has been approved by the FDA to prevent clotting in people who have already experienced a stroke or what healthcare professionals call "mini" episodes. Secondary strokes are more dangerous than many real

title: Compact smart telescope offers two views of the night sky
desc: Consumer Tech Technology By Monica J. White The Seestar S30 Plus is the new sibling to the S30 Pro, which we covered earlier this year. It's aimed at beginners and enthusiasts who want to capture the night sky without first having to spend hours assembling a mini-observatory.

title: VW Cubert mini-camper van is the chicest Caddy RV wandering roadways
desc: Campervans Adventure Vehicles Outdoors By C.C. Weiss Camper conversion shop Bodans takes the Caddy, Volkswagen's smallest van, and carves out a simple-but-elegant pop-up interior that's much more inviting than average. It's a cushy studio apartment on wheels in which you'll be happy to spend time.

title: Electric motorcycles are getting gearboxes - didn’t we get rid of those?
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood Single-speed transmissions on EVs are simple, efficient, and most of all, they work. But what if an electric moto could have the punch of shorter gearing and the legs of a taller ratio at higher speeds? Engineering firm E-Motiv might have the answer.

title: Cuboid camper doubles into proper tiny home & front porch of the wild
desc: By C.C. Weiss The X8 triple-expander wasn't the only all-new telescopic camper French innovator Beauer introduced this year. In its big lineup reshuffle, it also fully reshaped the future of its six-sleeper caravan. The all-new X6 breaks out of the curvaceous mold the brand has used exclusively for

title: Man sees his cat’s eyes in the faces of his friends after brain surgery
desc: Learning & Memory Brain Health Body and Mind By Mike McRae A recent case study describes the experiences of the 28-year-old man known only as Karl, providing researchers with a rare glimpse into how the human brain assembles faces and how memories can become entangled with what we see.

title: Solar-powered 'flying horse' radically slashes cost of irrigation
desc: Good Thinking Technology By Ben Coxworth High fuel prices may be no more than an inconvenience for most of us, but they can keep farmers in impoverished nations from making a living. A new vehicle has been designed to help, by using solar power to irrigate fields.

title: World's fastest car: BYD's 3,000-hp hypercar shatters 500-km/h barrier
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall Clocking 312.65 mph on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, BYD’s quad-motor Yangwang U9 Xtreme has become the first production car to crack 500 km/h, though the Guinness World Record is for a single pass only.

title: Space-saving tiny house sleeps six and packs a terrace up top
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams The roof of this tiny house does more than just keep the rain out: it also doubles as a terrace. Inside, the home features a clever space-saving interior layout that sleeps up to six people.

title: Electric comb could give thinning hair a chance to bounce back
desc: Medical Devices Medical Innovations Body and Mind By Mike McRae Researchers in China have given the humble comb an electric touch that has promoted regrowth among the remaining follicles in mice using little more than electricity and a dab of genetics.

title: 1,300-mile cargo drone aims to obsolete the helicopter
desc: Aircraft Transport By Omar Kardoudi Skyways' Skyreach hybrid VTOL takes off like a drone, cruises like a plane and burns jet fuel to stay up for more than 18 hours, delivering parts to offshore rigs and remote sites with with no pilot at the controls.

title: Iconic motorcycle builder bests Polaris and Can-Am at their own game
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall From Austria’s alpine foothills comes the extraordinary four-wheel-drive KTM X-Bow Arrow rally machine – with a 330-hp Audi turbo powertrain bolted into a brutal Dakar-spec chassis.

title: Slicey 5-in-1 flashlight smashes together 1,800 lumens & razor blade
desc: Knives and Multitools Gear Outdoors By C.C. Weiss Nitecore is moving its fast-growing ultra-slim flashlight family into all-out multitool territory. The UTL19 kicks off the new Utility Tool & Light series, going beyond mere illumination with hard tools that include a slide-out box-slicing blade.

title: A robot just built a structure in space for the first time
desc: By Mike McRae A robot designed by Caltech and funded by DARPA has recently demonstrated a potential solution to space construction by assembling an antenna’s truss from individual components in orbit.

title: Two-person tiny house provides hassle-free living on a single floor
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams Not every tiny house needs to be an exercise in squeezing as much as possible into the smallest footprint. The Cali 9.6 takes a more relaxed approach, with an easy to navigate single-floor layout that opens up to the outside.

title: Qantas Airbus A350-1000ULR sets world-record longest commercial flight
desc: Aircraft Transport By David Szondy Qantas Airways has entered the Guinness Book of World Records after the Fédération Aéronautique Internationale (FAI) verified that the airline's Airbus A350-1000ULR passenger liner completed the world's longest commercial flight from Melbourne to Toulouse.

title: Review: $100 blackout sound mask has changed my sleep game overnight
desc: Consumer Tech Technology By Bronwyn Thompson As a light sleeper who has been known to have a pillow or black shirt over my head in bed, while listening to a podcast or audiobook to drift off and stay that way, the Sleenova SleepMask has been a surprising game-changer.

title: Harley-Davidson launches its first US single-cylinder bike in 49 years
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood For all the heavy hitters in Harley-Davidson’s ranks, it is perhaps the Sprint 440 that has the biggest responsibility for carrying the weight of the company’s sales. For if H-D is able to hit home with its new motorcycle, it might well and truly be “back.”

title: Underwater ultrasound scans could help struggling coral reefs reproduce
desc: Imaging & Diagnostics Medical Innovations Body and Mind By Omar Kardoudi Ultrasound scanners usually spend their days giving expectant parents a first grainy look at their baby. Now Canon has pointed one of its machines at coral to see if it’s egg-laden, and to maybe help with its reproduction issue

title: Ford V8 crate engine brings unprecedented power to car of your choice
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall Ford Performance has revealed its most powerful competition crate engine ever: the Megazilla 2.0. It’s a twin-turbo 1,200-hp monster built to challenge the limits of aftermarket customization and bolt-on performance.

title: Road-ready tiny house packs a lot of flexibility into 26-ft-long frame
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams In a market packed with huge tiny houses, the Summer's Night Dream offers a refreshing change: a tiny house that's actually, well, tiny. Despite its modest dimensions, it sleeps four people – or even more at a squeeze.

title: Royal Enfield Himalayan 750: You asked for it, and it's finally here
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood After months of teasers and spy shots and what was effectively Royal Enfield’s poorest-kept secret, years of collective prayers have now been answered with the Himalayan 750. It’s here, it’s fresh, and it’s everything that the audience asked for.

title: New Atlas: Now available in Dark Mode :)
desc: By Loz Blain Some things just make me unreasonably happy, and I'm stoked to share this one: night owls like myself will appreciate the latest feature we've added to the site: a light/dark mode switch that should make New Atlas much easier on your eyes at night.

title: L-shaped tiny house embraces indoor/outdoor living
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams Most tiny houses take the form of a box shape, but the two-bedroom Antonia goes for a different approach. It's arranged in an L-shape around a terrace, creating a home designed to embrace indoor/outdoor living.

title: Space experiment shatters record for lowest temperature
desc: Materials Engineering By Mike McRae A cloud of atoms has been brought within a whisker of absolute zero in a recent space experiment, shattering the previous record in pursuit of the lowest possible temperatures.

title: Knee osteoarthritis pain relief – and massive weight loss – from new GLP-1
desc: Obesity Illnesses and Conditions Body and Mind By Bronwyn Thompson Two trials involving more than 1,000 adults has all but guaranteed Eli Lilly's experimental drug retatrutide will be up for FDA approval for weight loss and potentially even knee osteoarthritis pain relief. It's a GLP-1-based drug, b

title: MIT fuses best of Legos & Transformers into shape-shifting building blocks
desc: Electronics Consumer Tech Technology By Malcolm Azania New interactive, 3D-printed smart blocks are able to connect and maintain electrical conduction while transforming into new shapes. They can become video game controllers, medical-assistive tech, smart furniture, and soft-robotic grippers.

title: Shipping container-mountable guns offer plug-and-play naval defense
desc: Military Engineering By David Szondy Pirates attacking cargo ships might be in for a surprise in the near future as BAE Systems shows off its Sea Tridon family of 40-mm guns at the Euronaval 2026 exhibition in Paris. The systems are designed to be installed as easily as a shipping container.

title: New kit hoists boats out of the water for near-levitational foiling
desc: Marine Transport By Ben Coxworth All other things being equal, hydrofoils tend to be faster, more fuel-efficient and smoother-running than regular boats. But those regular boats needn't despair – there's now a kit that converts them into hydrofoils.

title: Battery-free sensor powers up wirelessly via local circuitry radiation
desc: Energy Engineering By Etiido Uko Thor, the Norse god of thunder, is famous for conjuring electricity from thin air. It turns out you don't need a magical hammer to do this, as scientists have created a device that harvests electricity from radiation in its environment.

title: France’s vision for the warship of 2040 packs lasers, railguns and drones
desc: Military Engineering By David Szondy The SCX 26, a vision of the warship of the 2040s, has been revealed by French shipbuilder Naval Group, complete with an unusual double superstructure, energy weapons, and advanced tech built to withstand the intense sea battles of tomorrow.

title: Weight loss is tied to earlier bedtime, not the hours spent asleep
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Whether it's four or eight hours, how much we sleep each night has become a focus of not just researchers but anyone looking to optimize their long-term health. However, a new study suggests we might be focusing on the wrong part of the clock.

title: Extra-wide tiny house gets comfortable cabin living just right
desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams A lot of tiny houses are designed for portability, but the Skye Park Model takes a different approach. It adopts an extra-wide frame to provide a much more spacious, apartment-like interior.

title: Mid-engine 3-wheeler packs more kilo-to-kilo power than a Ferrari Enzo
desc: Automotive Transport By Simon Heptinstall Unveiled at EICMA in Milan, the MTPeak One-All three-wheeler has retro style but premium supercar specs, with a mid-mounted turbocharged engine, carbon-fiber construction and track-worthy power-to-weight ratio.

title: 1-lb Japanese tent aims to be the lightest freestander anywhere
desc: Tents Gear Outdoors By C.C. Weiss Using some of the most advanced ultralight materials the world has at its disposal, Field Record offers the lightest freestanding tent we've ever seen. Its FR-SCD tent weighs less than half of many ultralight backpacking and mountaineering tents.

title: Magnetic modular display puts three adjustable screens in front of your face
desc: Computing Consumer Tech Technology By Maryna Holovnova For those of us who spend much of the day at a desk, there’s a new project on Kickstarter worth taking a look at. It’s a lightweight, modular display system that connects up to three additional monitors to a laptop with a single cable.

title: Solar plane soars to 47,600 ft, on target to fly 100 hours
desc: Aircraft Transport By Omar Kardoudi UAVOS says its solar-powered ApusNeo high-altitude platform recently flew for 29 hours over the Canary Islands, reaching 47,600 ft and running through the night on batteries, in a test aimed at keeping a permanent eye on wildfires.

title: Obituary: Tesla's Cybertruck (2023-2027)
desc: Automotive Transport By Bronwyn Thompson In news that won't come as a surprise to anyone besides those who drive one that hasn't had its wheels fall off, it's been announced that the Cybertruck's production is "winding down." In other words, it's being taken off life support for good.

title: Cold War bomber to get 21st-century hypersonic missile
desc: Military Engineering By David Szondy The cutting-edge future is meeting the over-engineered past as Lockheed Martin is awarded a US$694-million contract by the US Air Force to move the company's AGM-183A hypersonic missile to production for arming the vintage Cold War B-52 bomber.

title: Lollipop oral sensor will have your child excited for a checkup
desc: Good Thinking Technology By Maryna Holovnova Medical tests are no fun for anyone, but they might become less of bitter experience – quite literally. Researchers have developed a lollipop-inspired device designed to detect medication levels in saliva.

title: Three motorcycles that sound completely ridiculous but are real
desc: Motorcycles Transport By Utkarsh Sood All this talk of new motorcycles at EICMA with Android Auto and Apple CarPlay and displays as big as tablets and taglines like "future of mobility," and none of those bikes stand a chance against the three motorcycles we’ve dug out for you.

title: Your teeth could soon be protected by a futuristic force field
desc: By Mike McRae A new experimental brush gives tootbrush bristles a zap, using piezoelectric filaments to produce an electrical charge that drives a sterilizing chemical reaction to expose and damage the bacteria responsible for plaque and cavities.

title: New VW California camper van brings HUGE improvement at under 75K
desc: Campervans Adventure Vehicles Outdoors By C.C. Weiss Volkswagen gave its iconic California camper van a refresh earlier this year, adding a highly desirable new capability: climate control that runs off the plug-in hybrid battery for hours on end. The van is now officially available to order in the

title: Hopping, flying robot gets an all-terrain upgrade
desc: Robotics Engineering By Maryna Holovnova An upgraded hopping robot – Hopcopter – can handle everything from sandy dunes to icy roads. It stays stable, conserves energy, and can recover its balance after landing, potentially changing how we explore remote places or even other planets.

title: ONYX RCR 80V review: A 75mph electric moto with pedals, because laws exist

desc: Knives and Multitools Gear Outdoors By Shirl Leigh Most repair tools for the DIYer are functional, but can be cumbersome to carry around. The T.Fix, however – a triangular pocket-sized tool on Kickstarter – is a balance of function, versatility and modern elegant design.

desc: Tiny Houses Outdoors By Adam Williams One common way of maximizing space in a tiny house is by embracing an indoor/outdoor lifestyle. The Shak leans into this idea by opening up almost its entire interior to the outside – even including the bathroom.

title: 'World's 1st mass-produced humanoid robot' motors to market in China
desc: By Maryna Holovnova Chinese tech giant Ubtech has launched the 'world’s first' humanoid robot designed to be an everyday companion and live in your home. Despite ambitious claims, the product launch left many people more skeptical than impressed.

desc: 3D Printing Manufacturing Engineering By Malcolm Azania Human and mechanical error during design and printing leads to financially and ecologically expensive waste of 3D printing material. Yokohama University’s new method uses photodimerization to create meltable, reprintable tar-based resin.

title: Review: Solar-powered smart feeder offers bird's-eye view on your phone

desc: Motorcycles Transport By Abhimanyu Ghoshal In the event that the future is a dystopian hellscape with evil corporations ruling the world, it'd be pretty reasonable to turn to a life of crime, swiping data and selling cyborg spare parts on the black market. This is your era-appropriate ride.

desc: By Etiido Uko Man has occupied the ISS, orbiting at about 248 miles above sea level, for 25 years. Meanwhile, the sea, sitting at sea level, hasn’t had a fixed station manned for up to a month. Researchers are seeking to change that, with a new subsea habitat.

desc: Consumer Tech Technology By Abhimanyu Ghoshal RayNeo's Air 4 Pro glasses do one thing, and one thing only. Pop these on, plug them into your phone or laptop, and boom – an instant giant display for your eyes only. Movies and gaming on the go just got way more fun.

desc: Bicycles Transport By Abhimanyu Ghoshal N+ has developed a boatload of safety features – and licensed Volkswagen's branding – for its latest ebike. This baby has the first rear-view camera integrated into an ebike, and even talks to a smart helmet and glasses.

title: Porous compound pulls 2 liters of water from air, and is factory-ready

desc: Around The Home Consumer Tech Technology By Shirl Leigh From Smokpub, makers of a compact electric cocktail and whisky smoker, comes the Doubot, a sourdough fermentation system currently on Kickstarter. desc: By Simon Heptinstall Hyundai has launched the sleek Ioniq 3, a compact EV aimed at Europe’s busy small-car market. With up to 305 miles of range, fast charging and bold styling, the Renault 5, VW ID.3 and MG4 should be worried.

title: HiBreak Dual is an attempt at a more practical E Ink phone
desc: By Monica J. White Bigme’s HiBreak Dual combines a 6.13-inch E Ink display out front with a smaller LCD panel at the rear, aiming to reduce distractions while keeping core smartphone features like 5G, Android apps, and stylus support.

title: Bolt-action ratcheting screwdriver stores six bits in its revolving magazine
desc: By Ben Coxworth Let's be honest … tools that are made to be gun-like are generally pretty childish. They can also be practical at the same time, however, which is where the rifle-inspired Dream Knight ratcheting screwdriver comes in.

title: Ford Mustang GTD breaks Nürburgring record, and you can even buy one now
desc: By Utkarsh Sood You don’t just turn up at Nürburgring Nordschleife with an eye on Corvette ZR1X’s record. And who better to do it than the manufacturer who lost that record to Corvette itself? Well, Ford did exactly that with the new Ford Mustang GTD.

title: Latest glimpse of F/A-XX 6th-gen fighter reveals tailless design
desc: By David Szondy Northrop Grumman is teasing us again with another glimpse of its candidate for the US Navy's F/A-XX fighter program. The company posted a brief video on X (formerly Twitter) that gives the most complete look yet of the 6th-Gen aircraft.

title: Last day to grab $179 smart drill that puts workshop power in your hands
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Bridging the gap between portability and precision, the Spesyn Tool 3 is a smart cordless drill that's more like a workshop on-the-go. However, you only have a day left to grab it at US$179, 36% off, before its hugely successful launch campaign ends.

title: Robot smashes human record in half-marathon – as another self-destructed
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson A field of robots competing in a half marathon demonstrated how frighteningly fast the technology has developed in 12 months. Even if one bot had a race to forget, smashing into pieces at the starting line, Honor's Lightning instead smashed records.

title: Chainless recumbent ICE trike scraps the links for pedal-by-wire tech
desc: By Omar Kardoudi ICE Trikes' PERS Chainless setup turns pedaling into electricity, bringing pedal-by-wire tech to a production recumbent trike for the first time. Zero chain maintenance and over 30,000 miles before the drivetrain asks for anything.

title: Is Finland's new car-free bridge the longest of its kind in the world?
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Finland's just inaugurated its longest bridge, and not a single a car or motorcycle will ever be allowed on it. The Kruunuvuori Bridge is designed only for pedestrians, cyclists, and trams – and it's possibly the largest of its kind.

title: Self-improving AI model has people talking – for good reason
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson If it feels like AI is developing too fast to keep up with, a group of Chinese researchers have some bad news – because they've developed a model that "evolves" on its own, creating better versions of itself with each self-analytical loop.

title: Enclosed ebike uses retractable outriggers to keep riders on the upright
desc: By Ben Coxworth Fully-enclosed velomobiles may offer weather protection and an aerodynamic advantage over bicycles, but their three wheels do add weight and rolling resistance. The outrigger-equipped Manta ebike, however, takes a unique alternative approach.

title: New vision system trims the terror of "man overboard"
desc: By David Szondy "Man overboard!" is one of the most frightening things you can hear aboard ship and the outcome is often tragic. Now, maritime technology firm Zelim has achieved official certification for its ZOE Man-Overboard (MOB) machine-vision detection system.

title: 3/4-ounce tiny pod pump airs you up in just over 1 minute
desc: By C.C. Weiss One of the lightest, tiniest electric inflators available, the all-new AP01 bests Nitecore's previous micro-pumps with a weight of just 22 grams. Despite its small size, the potent pump can fill up a sleeping pad in just over a minute.

title: A life-saving upgrade for any bike helmet
desc: By Ben Coxworth While there are already bike helmets that provide vital wearer info in the event of a crash, they typically use electronics that must be built into the helmet. A new high-tech buckle, however, can simply be added to any existing helmet.

title: Japanese air-powered pillow has surprising impact on your day
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson This one-button self-adjusting pillow uses air pockets to gently shift your sleep position throughout the night – without waking you. it aims to eliminate the fatigue and "heaviness" that we feel in the morning, which becomes more common as we age.

title: How on earth is this insane 525hp go-kart street-legal?
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal You can now actually buy an Ariel Atom 4RR. The idea that one of these track weapons with 525 hp and a 0-60 mph time of just 2.4 seconds might actually be blasting through city streets has me gobsmacked.

title: Fearless rugged tablet packs projector, night vision and huge battery
desc: By Monica J. White The 8849 Tank Pad Ultra combines a built-in 1080p projector that puts out 260 lumens for on-the-spot visuals, as well as night vision cameras, and a laser rangefinder in a rugged tablet designed for fieldwork and outdoor use.

title: Scandi-style tiny house packs space-saving layout into just 270 sq ft
desc: By Adam Williams With its attractive wooden interior and minimalist design, the Scandi Inn wears its inspiration on its sleeve. Measuring just 270 sq ft, it makes the most of its compact footprint with space-saving ideas and lots of storage.

title: Review: 2026 Toyota Sienna takes minivan-ness to fat MPG levels
desc: By Aaron Turpen The most versatile vehicle on the road is the minivan and, like cargo shorts, it’s often maligned for no good reason. The 2026 Sienna expands that high practicality by adding a hybrid powertrain as the default.

title: Now we're cooking with water! Startup offers a hydrogen-powered stove
desc: By Etiido Uko Imagine slashing your cooking electricity bill by a factor of six. That would almost be as wild as cooking with water! Well, GreenVize says it has made both possible with a hydrogen-based cooking unit that runs on water and a bit of electricity.

title: Adaptable film camera shoots photos in any frame size you want
desc: By Shirl Leigh The VZ-6617 medium format camera, currently on Kickstarter, is a shortcut for the photographer eager to experiment with a range of formats for their landscape/scenic shots but hampered by the economics and restrictions of shooting one size at a time.

title: Review: Quality $35 headphones show this brand is no one-trick pony
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson In the running for best budget headphones of 2026, OneOdio's Focus A1 Pro outperform what you'd expect from a pair that'll set you back US$34.99. While they won't outshine premium audio tech, they leave the competition in their price bracket for dead.

title: Varmint round turns NATO rifles into drone killers
desc: By David Szondy With a simple switch of a magazine, the Drone Round is claimed to turn a standard NATO caliber small arm into a drone-killing weapon that combines the scattershot of a shotgun with the speed, power and rapid fire of an infantry assault rifle.

title: Focused microwaves allow 3D printers to fuse circuits onto almost anything
desc: By Omar Kardoudi A desktop-sized 3D printer can now write working electronic circuits directly onto a broad range of surfaces without burning them. The secret is microwaves, focused with surgical precision onto a spot no wider than a human hair.

title: Upside-down tiny house makes room for three bedrooms and two bathrooms
desc: By Adam Williams The Onda is a tiny house that tries something a little different. It turns the usual layout on its head to provide a roomy interior that places three bedrooms downstairs, and the main living area above.

title: Looking back: The liter-class Lamborghini superbike with a Kawasaki engine
desc: By Utkarsh Sood Everyone’s got a past, and Italian supercar maker Lamborghini is no different. Introduced in 1986, six prototype Design 90s superbikes came fitted with in-line four-cylinder Kawasaki engines. But here's the interesting bit: nobody wanted them.

title: Automated filtration system promises drinking water anywhere on demand
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal California-based startup Vital Lyfe says its first product, a portable battery-powered filtration system, can provide safe drinking water from any source on demand – including seawater. Expect as much as 12 gallons per hour, with no setup time.

title: Tiny house trades portability for a more spacious interior layout
desc: By Adam Williams The Lukas tiny house isn't a great fit for would-be nomads since it needs to be transported by truck. However, what it lacks in portability, it more than makes up for with a spacious interior that sleeps four in comfort.

title: Renpho Eyeris Zen massager review: It's surprisingly good
desc: By Joe Salas The last massager I bought was circa 2005, so I expected another failure that would simply annoy me and end up at Goodwill. Technology has changed a lot in 20 years, as I've found out with the Eyeris Zen.

title: Battery-boosted Mercedes super-saloon pushes closer to 600-mile range
desc: By Simon Heptinstall Mercedes has given its poshest electric saloon, the EQS, a mid-term refresh – showing exactly where the auto world’s current battleground is focused. Forget style, power, speed. Selling big EV sedans is now all about range.

title: Shoot ultra-smooth 4K at 240 fps with DJI’s newest pocket-sized gimbalcam
desc: By Monica J. White DJI’s Osmo Pocket 4 builds on its compact gimbal camera line with 4K/240fps video, improved tracking, refined imaging with boosted low-light performance, and smarter automation aimed at solo creators and on-the-go shooting.

title: Soft-top surfboard splits for travel and stowage
desc: By Maryna Holovnova WRocket is described as the first splittable soft-top surfboard, as it breaks down into three separate sections. Once disassembled, it fits into a relatively compact bag, making it much easier to travel with or store during the off-season.

title: Spacious single-level tiny house is built for nomadic life on wheels
desc: By Adam Williams The Esther features a spacious single-floor layout that sleeps up to two people. The tiny house is built with regular travel in mind and can run optionally off-grid, allowing its owners to cut the cord and embrace a nomadic lifestyle.

title: KTM somehow goes even harder with its 1390 Super Duke RR streetfighter
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal As if its flagship naked motorcycle didn't already pose enough risk to life and limb, KTM's gone and upped the ante with a limited edition variant. Only 350 of these will be made for over $40,000 a pop.

title: Breakthrough Kia pop-up tiny camper van is even slicker than expected
desc: By C.C. Weiss Less than two months after teasing the first Kia PV5 pop-up camper van, Sussex Campervans has revealed its work. The camper looks even better than expected, offering a sleek, rustic layout with sleeping, cooking, dining and even toilet amenities.

title: World-first eVTOL transition flight for Vertical Aerospace
desc: By David Szondy Vertical Aerospace has scored a world-first as its full-scale tilt-rotor eVTOL completed a two-way piloted transition between vertical helicopter mode and horizontal airplane mode during a single continuous flight while under regulatory oversight.

title: Honda's sporty compact EV includes simulated transmission sounds
desc: By Simon Heptinstall Honda has revealed intriguing details of forthcoming Super-One compact EV. Along with aggressive styling, up to 70 kW of motor power and a 200-mile city range, you can buckle up for an exciting simulated hot-hatch experience by hitting 'Boost.'

title: Forget scrubbing in the sink – this is a full-on shoe-washer and dryer
desc: By Maryna Holovnova Keeping shoes clean is neither easy nor particularly fun: hand scrubbing is ineffective, while regular washing machines are way too harsh. The Midishi M1 aims to make the process fully automated and quick, and it’s currently available on Kickstarter.

title: Surprisingly slim battery powers your fridge during hours-long outages
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Bluetti's stuffed a large-capacity home backup battery – designed specifically to keep your fridge running when the power goes out – into a compact shape that's easy to fit and forget right in your kitchen.

title: Shapeshifting camper van leaps beyond Swiss Army level
desc: By C.C. Weiss Plenty of camper vans boast multifunctional designs, but the Vanspeed Album takes it to new heights. What looks like an unassuming Sprinter camper is actually a transforming wonder, split into multipurpose zones that fold, drop, swivel and remove.

title: GoPro's new 8K Mission 1 camera is more than just an actioncam
desc: By Utkarsh Sood GoPro just stunned all of us by announcing a brand new line of action cameras. The Mission 1 won't replace the Hero lineup. Instead, it’s a new, parallel lineup that is aimed at pro creators who want to do more than just capture action in a jiffy.

title: Amazon's new Fire Stick HD is a no-brainer for frequent flyers
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Amazon's latest streaming device includes a handy feature that not only makes it a cinch to upgrade your old TV at home, but also to make long days on the road less of a drag. And it's just $35.

title: Instant, real-time video AI is now upon us, for better and worse
desc: By Loz Blain A new real-time video AI model was demonstrated yesterday, capable of generating its first frame in less than a tenth of a second. If you feel like the world's out of control right now and full of AI bullshit, just wait for what's coming.

title: Ingeniously prepped pop-up 4x4 camper wagon knows no bounds
desc: By C.C. Weiss Storyteller takes a break from adventure vans and huge RV trucks to launch an incredibly capable 4x4 micro-RV. Based on the Ineos Grenadier, the Grand Bohemian go-anywhere micro-camper is ready to explore the globe's hardest-to-reach expanses.

title: Low-cost hypersonic rocket engine takes flight for US Air Force
desc: By David Szondy The US Air Force is stomping on the accelerator to field advanced hypersonic missiles as the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) and Ursa Major announce the successful completion of a flight test of the mass-producible Draper liquid rocket engine.

title: BMW's sporty 3 series gets the electric Neue Klasse treatment
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal BMW is following through with its plan to apply the Neue Klasse design language to its entire all-electric lineup. You can now see it in the beloved 3 series, starting with the i3 50 xDrive electric sedan.

title: Mini rugged phone aims to be your essential adventure buddy
desc: By Paul Ridden Big screen, big battery and useful tools for outdoor enthusiasts – that's what we expect from rugged phones. But hefting one around can be like putting a brick in your pocket. Fossibot's latest effort shrinks the formula down a bit.

title: Smaller smart sensor gets the inside scoop on bike tire pressure
desc: By Ben Coxworth Checking the pressure of bike tires can be a hassle, particularly if you've got high-pressure tires that let out a gush of air every time you check. The Outrider TL Mini is here to help, as it sends wireless pressure readings from inside the tire.

title: Watch: Humanoid robot gets surprisingly good at tennis
desc: By Loz Blain This ain't teleoperation. Chinese researchers have tested a new, much quicker and easier method of teaching robots to play tennis, and the results look like a breakthrough in machine learning and real-world AI.

title: 24-ft-long tiny house expands living space with rooftop terrace
desc: By Adam Williams One of the obvious challenges with tiny houses is that living space is always so limited. The Erica addresses this with a rooftop terrace and an open interior layout. The home also has multiple options available, including adding in solar power.

title: $23K razor-framed bicycle wears surprise badging all over
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Snapping up the most basic supercar Bugatti makes will set you back by about two and a half million dollars. An easier five-figure entry into the legendary Italian marque's client list is the new aero bicycle it's collaborated on with Factor Bikes.

title: Smart hub is made to keep bike and moto bars sleek and simple
desc: By Ben Coxworth Although bar-mounted smartphones are a common sight, we're seeing an increasing number of compact simplified devices designed specifically for two-wheelers. The turn-by-turn navigating RC10 is the latest, and it even sports a headlight.

title: Retro reusable digicam draws on the spirit of the disposable film camera
desc: By Shirl Leigh The Rewindpix, a non-disposable digital camera currently on Kickstarter, is a throwback to the single-use film cameras for people who missed the 90s the first time around, now that the era is vibing all over again.

title: Legendary RV brand reinvents everyday carry essential
desc: By Simon Heptinstall Dometic’s modular Drinkware system combines a range of bottles, lids and accessories into 408 configurations for any liquid carrying use you can think of, from everyday hydration to serious outdoor adventures.

title: 12-sided skyscraper sets record for most floors in North America
desc: By Adam Williams The ambitious Pinnacle SkyTower has reached a major milestone. The supertall skyscraper has topped out at 106 floors and now holds the record for the most floors of any residential building in North America.

title: Laser-fused 'glass' motor improves drive efficiency
desc: By Etiido Uko When you think of glass, you probably picture something fragile and brittle, not a material built for high-stress electromechanical components. Yet researchers are significantly improving the efficiency of electric motors by using “glass” parts!

title: Battery lasts a week, broken wrists are forever – Oukitel WP61 Plus
desc: By Joe Salas To get straight to the point: This rugged smartphone packs a 20,000-mAh battery, doubles as a walkie-talkie, and includes a 1,200-lumen camp light ... but it's nearly the same size and weight as an actual brick.

title: FAA greenlights eVTOL aircraft operations across the USA
desc: By Loz Blain Nearly three years after China began certifying next-gen electric "air taxis" for commercial flights, American contenders are still battling red tape with the FAA – but a new accelerator program will get them airborne across the USA this summer.

title: Everything you need to go off the grid fits in this $35,000 teepee
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal This ominous-looking structure could make it way easier to set up your truly private homestead in the middle of nowhere. The Klumpen features a host of utilities including solar power and HVAC ready to go in just 24 hours.

title: Tech-packed cargo ebike puts eyes in the back of your head
desc: By Monica J. White The Tarran L1 cargo ebikes combine radar sensing, an auto kickstand, and smart integrations to make heavily loaded urban riding easier. Designed for families and commuters, they focus on stability, safety, and usability over raw performance.

title: 30-sec iron-jawed strong box camper hammers into next-gen 4x4 camping
desc: By C.C. Weiss Perhaps no one brand better exemplifies Australia's off-road camping trailer mastery better than Track Trailer and its Tvan. The jawy little hammerhead camper now rolls out in its sixth iteration, gaining a roomier, more comfortable camping pod.

title: Apple's AirPods Max 2 delivers better ANC, plays catch-up with rivals
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Apple has refreshed its AirPods Max headphones with new internals for better performance, as well as a handful of features that bring it in line with current-gen over-ear models – for the same price as the original.

title: Aprilia's new crossover scooter: Part adventure, part sports bike
desc: By Utkarsh Sood Few companies do sportbikes like Aprilia. Of late, the Italian brand has expanded into other segments, most notably the adventure motorcycle category. Now, a new crossover scooter combines elements from both those styles.

title: Rippling glass facade adds drama to Queensland's new cultural center
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal There's a whole giant structure with remarkable details behind the glass, but we're all really here for this building's striking facade. This is the Glasshouse Theatre, a new performance venue unveiled last week in Brisbane.

title: Swedish electric PWC is ready to take you on a sustainable aquatic jet ride
desc: By Maryna Holovnova Roxen Innovations, a Swedish company focused on sustainable water vehicles, has announced its Roxen electric personal watercraft (PWC). It’s designed to be quiet, lightweight, and environmentally friendly without compromising performance.

title: Amazing architecture images from the Sony World Photography Awards 2026
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Architecture is a bit of an underrated photo competition category but it is one that can simultaneously capture design, engineering and human experience. We pick our 2026 Sony World Photography Awards’ Professional finalist and shortlist standouts.

title: Review: The Bear 650 is the one Royal Enfield everyone is sleeping on
desc: By Utkarsh Sood It’s been a minute since Royal Enfield launched the scrambler-style Bear 650. And while you’d think Enfield simply revised some bodywork of the Interceptor 650, slapped some knobby tires on, and said voila, there’s more to it than meets the eye.

title: Mini Roomba robovac cleans and mops where others can't
desc: By Stefan Ionescu iRobot has launched the Roomba Mini, a small robot that vacuums and mops. It maps spaces in 10 minutes, can squeeze into tight spaces, boosts suction on thick carpets, and auto-empties into a sealed bag that lasts for up to 90 days.

title: Tiny house proves you can downsize without compromising comfort
desc: By Adam Williams Created for a pair of nomads who were looking to put down roots, the Coastal Retreat is a remarkably spacious tiny house that proves that downsizing doesn't always have to mean sacrificing home comforts.

title: Space-age photo frame displays your family pictures as holograms
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Looking Glass has been in the holographic display business for years now, perfecting its tech for magically bringing images to life in commercial settings. Its latest product is designed to grace your living room – and it doesn't cost the earth.

title: Tiny threads stand in for major metal coils in heating breakthrough
desc: By Michael Franco Could tiny threads of carbon fiber do the same job as big metal industrial heating coils? A new breakthrough from researchers at Rice University says yes, and the finding could go a long way toward electrifying many manufacturing processes.

title: Radical recumbent trike is powered by arms, legs, or both at once
desc: By Ben Coxworth Cycling is a great form of exercise for the legs and core, but the arms? Not so much. The VeloGym recumbent trike is out to change that, as it gets your upper body in on the act.

title: Off-grid tiny office has two separate workspaces and even a bed
desc: By Adam Williams This interesting "tiny house" isn't actually a house at all. Instead, it's a mobile off-grid office that squeezes two separate workspaces, plus a sleeping area, into its compact frame. It's currently up for sale for $98,000.

title: DAB electric supermoto makes a strong case to be your first e-moto
desc: By Utkarsh Sood DAB Motors has launched its very first mass-production e-moto called the DAB 1. And as the name suggests, it’s based on the exclusive DAB 1α. And unlike its predecessor, this one’s a standard run, and more importantly, significantly cheaper.

title: Futuristic mouse snaps in half to transform into a gamepad
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal A Bangalore, India-based hardware upstart is rethinking what the mouse on your desk can do – by splitting it in two and filling it with gamepad buttons. It's a clever bit of industrial design that hides interface elements in a familiar package.

title: Tech-giant partnership promises faster deployment of humanoids
desc: By Michael Franco Texas Instruments has teamed up with NVIDIA to link technologies designed to "accelerate the path from simulation to the safe deployment of humanoid robots in the real world." The partnership fuses real-world sensing tech with massive computing power.

title: Folding hard cooler carries 93 cans, then smashes flat to store tiny
desc: By C.C. Weiss Coleman takes hard coolers in a new direction it qualifies as a world first. The Snap 'N Go series comprises nicely squared cooler boxes that stack and store neatly when full and even more neatly after instantly folding down to a fraction their size.

title: Yashica's $100 'Tank' pays homage to early digital cameras
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Yashica's turned back time to get inspiration for its latest camera, the Tank. It's a pocketable little shooter that's all about keeping things simple and letting you engage with your craft behind the lens, like with early digital cameras.

title: Ambitious startup plans to put AI data centers in offshore wind turbines
desc: By Etiido Uko What do you get when you combine distressed offshore wind energy sites, surging AI energy demands, and not-in-my-backyard sentiments towards data centers? One company is combining all three problems into a solution: floating offshore data centers.

title: Researchers crack the physics of dangerous battery dendrites
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson Researchers have uncovered the mechanical properties of the nanoscale "thorns" that grow inside lithium batteries, which can cause them to short circuit or even combust. This paves the way to stop these growths forming, preserving battery power.

title: This dinghy shrinks to two bags and expands into a family sailing trip
desc: By Omar Kardoudi The Tiwal 2XL is a family-sized inflatable sailboat that's ready for the water in under half an hour, and deflates into two bags for transport in the trunk of a regular family car – no marina or mooring required.

title: Otherworldly capsule camper explodes into base camp at push of button
desc: By C.C. Weiss Skydream Caravans aims to build next-generation travel trailers that integrate cutting-edge advances from China's new energy, automotive and smart home sectors. Its debut caravan is about to drop down like something of a terrestrial spacecraft.

title: Rivian's R2 SUV comes in at $45,000 – but you'll have to wait
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal EV darling Rivian has just announced pricing for its R2 SUV that it unveiled to great fanfare back in 2024. The company is indeed making a $45,000 variant as promised – but that'll arrive only toward the end of 2027.

title: Tiny house packs surprisingly capable interior into 320 sq ft
desc: By Adam Williams Despite its length of just 30 ft, the Elderberry tiny house packs a surprisingly capable interior. The towable dwelling includes a living area with a home office, two lofts, and a spacious central kitchen.

title: Torque-rich e-moto has 60-mile range, 50-mph top speed – all for $1,899
desc: By Utkarsh Sood In an age where electric bike launches are becoming bigger, faster, heavier, and inherently more expensive, the IN10 Pro+ is the exact opposite. For under $2,000, it just might be a masterstroke!

title: EyeDAR tech could give self-driving cars expanded radar perception
desc: By Etiido Uko Many cultures explore the idea of a figurative third eye that enhances perception. Autonomous cars have a literal version: radar, working alongside cameras and LiDAR. Now, scientists are pushing the idea further by placing that third eye on the road.

title: BMW's first Neue Klasse EV is here, and it divides opinions
desc: By Utkarsh Sood The first of BMW's Neue Klasse EVs debuts in the form of the iX3. It gives us a first look at BMW’s next-generation cars, while also shedding light on what we can expect from its upcoming range that will launch between now and this time next year.

title: 1-oz pico pump airs up entire base camp in minutes
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Adventure gear brand Outzac has a new piece of camping equipment in the works that's designed to make it way easier to pack light, in more ways than one. The Pico Pump is compact, inflates all your stuff, and can shrink your packing in vacuum bags.

title: Aptera solar EV rolls off assembly line for the first time
desc: By Simon Heptinstall It has been a long, twisting journey for Aptera’s solar-powered electric vehicle, but we can at last report that the extraordinary futuristic car has taken a huge step toward mass production.

title: $39k tiny house fits full-time living into 16 ft length
desc: By Adam Williams How much can you realistically fit into a tiny house measuring just 16 ft in length? You might assume the answer is "not much," but this model squeezes in a surprisingly effective space-saving layout – and does so at a low cost.

title: Apple's lo-fi MacBook Neo gets an iPhone chip and a tempting price tag
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Over a decade after the compact 12-inch MacBook, Apple's taking another stab at an entry-level laptop with the MacBook Neo. Powered by a processor from a previous-generation iPhone, it's meant for people who mostly get things done in their browser.

title: Carbon Mercedes super-Sprinter foreshadows spacious camper bus future
desc: By C.C. Weiss A new type of van for a new type of camper, the Reiter Orca sees a bony Mercedes Sprinter chassis transformed into a high-capacity ultralight transporter positively starving for gear, tools, RV furnishings or whatever else you want to stuff in.

title: Pop-on digi-cam brings new life to old film cameras
desc: By Shirl Leigh Could the Ligar digital camera resurrect your obsolete vintage film camera? Currently crowdfunding on Kickstarter, the device pops onto any film camera with a hot-shoe connection, allowing users to shoot both film and digital images simultaneously.

title: Xiaomi's 1,900 HP Vision GT electric hypercar breaks cover, and it's a looker
desc: By Utkarsh Sood There was a time when the name Xiaomi was synonymous with home appliances. Now, the company has pulled the covers off a 1,900-hp electric hypercar concept called the Vision Gran Turismo. And it is breathtakingly beautiful!

title: Titanium pocket tool bends four ways to ratchet drive any screw
desc: By Omar Kardoudi The Arcos Driver aerospace-grade titanium pocket tool can crack even the most elusive screw. It packs a four-angle articulating head and three-mode ratchet into a 2.5-oz frame. If it ships as built, it might be the last screwdriver you pocket.

title: Guess which brand sells 70% of all e-motorcycles sold in the US
desc: By Utkarsh Sood We’re probably all aware of Harley-Davidson’s struggles of late. It’s electric offshoot LiveWire hasn’t fared too well, either. Though the company reportedly sold three-quarters of all e-motos in the USA in 2025. But there’s a big caveat there.

title: Two-wheel-drive hybrid Yamaha MT-07 comes with hub-mounted front motor
desc: By Utkarsh Sood This custom-made Yamaha Mt-07 is an all-wheel-drive model, thanks to an additional electric motor on the front wheel. You get an axial flux design, with coils, a magnet, and two discs. The end result? Close to 221 lb-ft on the front wheel!

title: Foam-core camper canopy reimagines truck camping ... and pricing
desc: By C.C. Weiss Tekton introduces a different style of camping canopy, leaving aluminum behind and applying the composite expertise it honed on small trailers. Its monocoque CX then builds into a proper Outback survival tool via an ecosystem of optional add-ons.

title: Mammal-inspired skin sweats to keep batteries cool
desc: By Etiido Uko Li-ion batteries need complex cooling systems. Yet, the human body, which generates enough heat to boil over 100 cups of tea daily, is literally just chillin’. The secret? Our skin’s ability to sweat. Scientists may have given batteries this ability.

title: Tiny house trades portability for generous outdoor living space
desc: By Adam Williams Though most tiny houses we see are designed with nomadic living in mind, the Forest is semi-permanently installed on rural land. It expands its compact interior footprint with a large deck that includes a porch area and a rooftop terrace.

title: Retro-inspired pocket tool adds vice-like grip to every project
desc: By Maryna Holovnova A compact, British-designed clamping tool is seeking backing on Kickstarter. The Pocket Grip from MetMo is lightweight, pocket-sized, and inspired by a century-old prototype.

title: Forgotten bikemaker comes back with parallel-twin neoclassic café racer
desc: By Utkarsh Sood While the name is about the same, the 730 Twin is a neoclassic café racer that is not from the production line of the Jawa-Yezdi-Mahindra group in India, but from Jawa Moto in the Czech Republic – the brand that started it all.

title: Privacy-focused phone runs Android apps without intrusive tracking
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Finnish smartphone brand Jolla isn't in the business of competing with the dizzying array of Android handsets out there. In fact, it took a long break before announcing its latest model – but from the sound of things, it might be worth the wait.

title: Temperature-sensitive tires automatically deploy retractable studs
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Finnish tire brand Nokian has launched a winter tire that features studs which deploy only when it's cold out – so they bite into the ice and give you better traction. It's all thanks to a proprietary 3-layer construction technology.

title: Cozy 200-sq-ft tiny house offers simple small living from $50K
desc: By Adam Williams Mysa is the Swedish word for "cozy," which is a fitting name for this affordable cabin-like tiny house. Designed as a compact but extra-wide non-towable home, it would suit being used as a vacation retreat or a guesthouse.

title: Australia launches 3D-printed, Mach 8 hypersonic missile from US soil
desc: By David Szondy Australia's Hypersonix Launch Systems has made a historic launch of its next-generation DART AE hypersonic aircraft from Wallops Island, Virginia. Taking off aboard Rocket Lab's HASTE launch vehicle, the DART AE reached a top speed of Mach 8.

title: Clever cycling gadget puts power metering where your cleat is
desc: By Ben Coxworth Traditional power meters are mounted on just one bike, limiting their use to that particular vehicle. Such is not the case with the cleat-integrated CycloWatt, however, which can be used with as many road bikes as you can lay your hands on.

title: Radical expander camper cracks open into family-size mini-lodge
desc: By C.C. Weiss Berg shook up the camper scene when it introduced the CX6, a neat squaredrop that expands out in every direction to create a huge base camp for 6 people. Now it's packaged that same shell into a 3-/4-person camper sized perfectly for a family.

title: Everything new in Apple's 2026 MacBook Pro and MacBook Air laptops
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal The new MacBook Air and MacBook Pro are great for most people and for demanding users respectively – but as much as Apple has raised the bar with these, they're just incremental improvements that aren't worth upgrading from the previous models.

title: Quarterhorse 2.1 takes flight on way to beating 50-year-old SR-71 record
desc: By David Szondy Aerospace startup Hermeus has taken another step toward challenging the Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird’s legendary supersonic speed record as the company’s uncrewed Quarterhorse Mk 2.1 lifted off from Spaceport America in New Mexico on March 2, 2026 for its maiden flight.

title: Two days left to save 71% on this hit carry-on that's raised $1.2M from fans
desc: By Bronwyn Thompson As someone who's spent the year living in five countries, I now see why quality luggage is worth the investment. And it's why I'm excited about the debut of this titanium case – which has nearly 2,000 backers. It's also 71% off for two more days.

title: Bonkers omnidirectional electric 'bike' balances on a single ball wheel
desc: By Omar Kardoudi The latest mobility build from British inventor James Bruton is his most unhinged yet. He sits on a huge single ball that moves him in any direction, steered – for now – by a hot-glued foam fin. Not a balance bike as such, more a big-ball unicycle.

title: 28-ft tiny house hits sweet spot between portability and livability
desc: By Adam Williams The Betty sits in a nice mid-size spot that's a good compromise between portability and spaciousness. The tiny house provides a well-planned interior layout designed for two, including a proper ground-floor bedroom and a loft for storage.

title: Ingenious invention turns wheelchair users into Steadicam operators
desc: By Shirl Leigh The Caerus Steadicam was initially designed for wheelchair users to work in the film industry, but there are advantages also for the able-bodied since the weight distribution is spread out on the wheelchair, and there's no need for tracks or dollies.

title: Gerber retools camp multi-plier to bridge backcountry with backyard
desc: By C.C. Weiss Since launching the Stakeout multitool in 2022, Gerber has grown the family with new tools and tweaks. This year, it's released the Stakeout Drive, a multi-plier with flip-out driver meant to seamlessly shift from weekday DIY to weekend adventure.

title: Intermittent fasting fails to live up to its weight-loss hype in new study
desc: By Michael Franco News about intermittent fasting seems to change as frequently as the apps on your phone need upgrading. Yet another new study about the eating practice seeks to put doubts to rest after rounding up data from 22 randomized clinical trials.

title: Torquey adventure ebike auto engages mid-drive muscle to tame trails
desc: By Monica J. White Aventon’s Ramblas ADV e-MTB steps firmly into trail territory with a new 750-W mid-drive motor delivering 100 Nm of torque. Launching at $2,899, it bridges the gap between value ebikes and premium mid-drive mountain brands.

title: New video may offer glimpse of secret F-47 fighter
desc: By David Szondy In what may be a hint of things to come or a subtle act of disinformation, Pratt & Whitney has released a video possibly featuring a tantalizing new image of the Boeing F-47 sixth-generation fighter plane being developed for the US Air Force to replace the F-22.

title: Lenovo's wild gaming handheld concept unfolds into a laptop
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Windows gaming handhelds are having a moment, as the form factor conveniently lets you enjoy your PC games away from your desk. Lenovo's already been cooking up solid options, but its latest concept may be the most compelling one yet for multitaskers.

title: Family friendly tiny house packs three bedrooms into 32-ft layout
desc: By Adam Williams With its Avalon 32', Dragon Tiny Homes has revealed an all-new tiny house that's ready for full-time family living. It features a spacious interior layout that manages to pack three bedrooms into a towable interior.

title: Long-tail cargo ebike has everything families need to go car-free
desc: By Stefan Ionescu The Swoop ASM is a long-tail cargo ebike designed for families, offering high payload capacity, a smooth ride, a Shimano EP-6 motor, automatic shifting, powerful brakes, and included accessories. Pre-orders start at $4,499 including launch discounts.

title: 3D-printed cave home: Rock the modern Flintstones lifestyle
desc: By Adam Williams Described as Japan's first two-story 3D-printed home, the O House is inspired by cave structures. Built to meet the country's strict seismic requirements, it combines cutting-edge robotic construction with earthquake-resistant engineering.

title: Google spinoff beams blazing-fast internet around cities using light
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Taara has been developing tech to deliver connectivity across communities without underground cables over the last few years. For its latest trick, the Google spinoff is now providing fast internet access across cities using invisible beams of light.

title: World first Kia pop-up tiny camper changes the face of van life
desc: By C.C. Weiss The first camper kit developed specifically for Kia's PV5 van hit the market a couple weeks ago, and now we have the world's first pop-up PV5 production camper. Sussex's pop-top PV5 promises to open up new heights of Kia electric base camping.

title: Century-old 1,172cc flat-four moto could go for over $100,000 at auction
desc: By Utkarsh Sood The Holden comes with a gargantuan 1,172.8cc flat-four engine; one of the earliest experiments in high-cylinder motorcycle design. Bonhams takes this example to auction in April , and pre-show estimates sit between £40,000 and £70,000.

title: This university's roof is a massive 9,000-seat open auditorium
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Indian studio Sanjay Puri Architects dreamed up plans for a university that are quite unlike the usual imposing structures that immediately come to mind. It's a marvel from every angle, and especially so when you look at the roof.

title: Epson's 4K Lifestudio hub turns projection into a design centerpiece
desc: By Monica J. White Epson’s Lifestudio Flex Special Lux Edition EF-73 pairs 4K PRO-UHD projection with a sleek exterior and a wireless charger. Built for daily living rather than dark-room cinema, it aims to make projection a seamless part of modern home decor.

title: Two small-but-unique knives vie for enthusiasts' attention on Kickstarter
desc: By Maryna Holovnova There seems to be an unspoken competition in the everyday-carry (EDC) world right now: who can create the most unique compact knife? Two projects currently on Kickstarter are battling for the attention of EDC enthusiasts.

title: 2026 DesertX gets Ducati's lightest twin-cylinder engine ever
desc: By Abhimanyu Ghoshal Ducati's given its beloved DesertX adventure motorcycle a major overhaul, with a view to enhance off-road performance. There are both thoughtful updates and possibly controversial trade-offs for fans of the outgoing model.

title: Visitor center embedded in extinct volcanic landscape
